frame_89.jpg.note: The figures are blocky, low-poly, stick-limbed and identical, with flat painted-on details like the blue X. They march in a rigid grid on a huge empty tiled floor. The scale reads as tabletop miniatures or game pieces. Contact shadows are minimal and the walk poses are stiff and copy-pasted.

frame_65.jpg.note: These are rigid A-pose mannequins. The 1782 coat is flat and unfolded, with a hollow-looking torso and a bare crotch seam. The 1943 uniform looks like a skin-tight onesie with no fabric folds. Hands and feet are crude, the shoes look like rubber boots, the faces are blank or have glitchy eyes, and the neck and cuff seams are jagged. The anatomy is fairly proportionate and the shading is soft, so they read as video-game or doll figures more than literal toys. They still don't read as real people.
